findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,"minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset,"minutes")` compares two distinct Dayjs object instances with strict equality, which is always `false` regardless of the actual timestamps, so the intended "full-day-blocked override" fast path is dead code (impact is largely masked because a zero-width override window is still caught by the subsequent isBefore/isAfter checks on lines 117-125, but the code does not do what its logic implies)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:140 — workingHour.days.includes(...)` and `dateOverrides`/`workingHours` entries are accessed with no validation/try-catch around the new find() callbacks, so a malformed entry (e.g. `days` undefined) would throw inside `Array.prototype.find`, propagating an uncaught exception out of `checkIfIsAvailable` and failing the whole `getSchedule` request instead of failing safe (blocking just that slot)

goldens.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `workingHours.find((workingHour) => workingHour.days.includes(...))` and iterates `dateOverrides`, but nothing in the shown changes indicates these arrays can contain malformed entries (e.g. `days` undefined). `workingHours` comes from `getAggregateWorkingHours(...)` and `dateOverrides` is built from `availability.dateOverrides` (DB-shaped) plus a `timeZone`. The finding asserts a new, diff-introduced uncaught-exception path due to malformed data, but that risk is speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,"minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset,"minutes")` compares two freshly-constructed dayjs objects by reference, which is always false, so a full-day-blocked override (start equal to end) never triggers the "unavailable" branch and fails to block the day

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new date override logic does `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")) { return true; }`. This compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, which will never be true, so the intended special-case for `start === end` (used here to trigger the outer `find(...)` and return `false` => unavailable) will not execute. As a result, when an override has equal start/end on the matching day, `dateOverrideExist` becomes true and the function falls through to `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`, incorrectly marking slots available.
